body: Organigram Global Inc. has agreed to acquire Aurora Cannabis Inc. in a transaction the companies valued at approximately $561 million, offering Aurora shareholders $7.80 per share. The offer follows several months in which Aurora had been fending off a hostile takeover attempt from Curaleaf Holdings Inc., based in Stamford, Connecticut, according to the companies.

Aurora shareholders will be able to elect one of three forms of consideration: cash only, 5.86 Organigram shares for each Aurora share, or a combination of $3.75 in cash and 3.04 Organigram shares. Organigram's offer represents a roughly 21-per-cent premium to Curaleaf's latest bid of US$5 a share, the companies said.

The transaction requires approval from at least two-thirds of the votes cast by Aurora shareholders at a special meeting expected to take place in December for the deal to proceed, the companies said.

Organigram is funding the acquisition through a $188-million private placement with British American Tobacco and $210 million in loan facilities from ATB Financial, the companies said. If the deal receives shareholder approval, the combined company would operate five EU-GMP certified facilities.

On the venture boards, the cannabis theme comprises eight listed venture names. Two traded today, none higher and one lower, for a median move of -2.17 per cent against -0.77 per cent for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of -1.40 percentage points between the theme and the broader venture board.

Decibel Cannabis Company Inc. (TSXV: DB) was unchanged at C$1.80, and is included in the theme because its registered name contains "cannabis." The move falls on the same trading day as the Organigram-Aurora announcement; nothing in the day's trading data establishes a connection between the two.
